findings.body:
`0008` depends on `("billing", "0007_add_reason")`, but this PR deletes `migrations/0007_add_reason.py`. Django builds the graph from migration files on disk, so the loader will fail with `NodeNotFoundError` (or similar) on `migrate` / `showmigrations` — nothing in the tree provides `0007_add_reason` or a replacement edge from `0006_initial`.

**Fix:** If `0007` has been applied anywhere, restore that file and keep this `RemoveField` migration as a normal forward drop. If `0007` was never applied anywhere, drop this file entirely and only delete `0007` (no `0008` needed).

Deleting an existing numbered migration rewrites history. Any database that already applied `billing.0007_add_reason` will have that row in `django_migrations` and the `void_reason` column present, while the codebase no longer ships the migration file — Django then cannot reconcile recorded history with the graph (missing node, inconsistent plan).

Even when the column is unused in the UI, the safe contract is: leave `0007` in place and add a new `RemoveField` migration. Only delete `0007` if you have proof it was never applied on any shared or local DB, and in that case do not add a follow-up `0008` that depends on it.

`RemoveField` drops the column and permanently discards any stored values. The comment only claims the field was never shown in the UI — that does not prove the column is empty in production or that no API/admin/shell wrote to it.

Before merging a forward drop (with `0007` restored), confirm no rows rely on `void_reason`, or accept explicit data loss in the PR risks section. If the add never shipped, delete `0007` instead of running `RemoveField`.

summary:
## Verdict

Do not merge — the migration graph is broken and will fail on every environment that runs `migrate`.

## What went wrong

This PR deletes `migrations/0007_add_reason.py` (the migration that added `invoice.void_reason`) and adds `migrations/0008_drop_reason.py`, which still declares:

```python
dependencies = [("billing", "0007_add_reason")]
```

Django loads the graph from files on disk. With `0007` gone, `0008` points at a missing node, so `manage.py migrate` / `showmigrations` raises `NodeNotFoundError` (or an equivalent loader error). The working tree after this PR contains only `0008_drop_reason.py`, so there is no path from `0006_initial` either.

## Correct approaches

Pick one based on whether `0007` has ever been applied:

1. **Already applied anywhere (prod, staging, a teammate DB):** restore `0007_add_reason.py` and ship only `0008` as a forward `RemoveField`. Never delete a migration that may be recorded in `django_migrations`.
2. **Never applied anywhere:** delete `0007` only and do **not** add `0008`. There is nothing to drop if the add never ran.

The comment that `void_reason` was never surfaced in the UI does not justify rewriting history; UI absence does not mean the column is empty on applied databases, and `RemoveField` still drops whatever values exist.

## Secondary note

No model, app package, or earlier migrations are in this repo slice, so application-level references could not be fully audited beyond a repo-wide search (no remaining `void_reason` hits outside the new migration). The graph break is independently fatal.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
